title: Health Education Methods
topics: Nature and purpose of the field
Working with individuals face to face

items.q: Which of the following best describes Billboard?
o: a formal talk delivered to a large body of listeners with little exchange
a large outdoor board carrying a painted or pasted message beside a road
a single folded sheet of printed matter given out by hand
the study carried out to discover what a group lacks and wants to know
items.s: Billboard: a large outdoor board carrying a painted or pasted message beside a road. The other options describe Leaflet, Needs assessment, Lecture.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Prototype.
o: the first working version of a material, made to be tested and revised
a large outdoor board carrying a painted or pasted message beside a road
information given to a learner about how well an action was performed
the telling of a narrative whose events carry the message across to listeners
items.s: Prototype: the first working version of a material, made to be tested and revised. The other options describe Billboard, Storytelling, Feedback.

items.q: The statement “the study of the age, literacy and interests of those to be addressed” describes which of the following?
o: Lesson plan
Instructional objective
Audience analysis
Time allocation
items.s: Audience analysis is the study of the age, literacy and interests of those to be addressed.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Observation checklist?
o: a pair or trio that talks over one question briefly before the whole gathering resumes
the length of time and accuracy with which what was learned is kept available
a list of behaviours ticked as they are seen being performed
the body of principles governing how children are taught
items.s: Observation checklist: a list of behaviours ticked as they are seen being performed. The other options describe Pedagogy, Retention, Buzz group.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Learning style.
o: repeated practice of one action until it can be done without hesitation
the tongue spoken in the home area, preferred for reaching ordinary residents
the preferred way an individual takes in and processes new material
a life-size model of the body used for practising procedures
items.s: Learning style: the preferred way an individual takes in and processes new material. The other options describe Manikin, Skill drill, Local language.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Content outline.
o: the choice of simple local equipment that can be maintained where it is used
the relatively permanent change in knowledge, attitude or skill that follows experience
the ordered list of what will be covered within a session
a station owned and run by a locality, broadcasting in the local tongue
items.s: Content outline: the ordered list of what will be covered within a session. The other options describe Learning, Appropriate technology, Community radio.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Motivation?
o: a list of behaviours ticked as they are seen being performed
the share of the available period given to each part of a session
a large outdoor board carrying a painted or pasted message beside a road
the inner drive that moves a person to begin and persist in an activity

Panel
